newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Health buys Coram for $655 mln.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Health buys Coram for $655 mln.

text.p: Integrated Health Services Inc said Monday it had entered a definitive merger agreement with Coram Healthcare to acquire the company.

Integrated said its $655 million acquisition would create what it described as the country's second largest home health company and largest post-acute care company including services like home nursing.
Integrated said it would pay Coram stockholders $5.50 in value in its common stock for each share they owned of Coram common stock with a fixed exchange rate.
It said it would issue 0.2111 shares of its common stock for each share of Coram common stock and -- when the acquisition was complete -- issue about 10.8 million shares of common stock.

Integrated said the equity value of the merger, which is to close during the first quarter of next year, was about $280 million, based on the exchange terms. The total value of the transaction, including the assumptions of Coram's debt and other financial obligations, was about $655 million, it said.
Integrated said it expected the merger to be accretive to its earnings per share in 1997 and afterwards if it were to exclude the transaction costs.
Coram, which provides home intravenous therapy, has annual revenues of $532 million and 112 locations in 43 states.

Integrated also said it had negotiated a settlement of the litigation involving Coram and Caremark International, a wholly owned subsidiary of MedPartners Inc. Under the settlement, notes of about $111 million that are payable by Coram to Caremark will be cancelled and replaced with a new two-year note in the principal amount of $57.5 million, it said.
Integrated said the lawsuit stemmed from the sale of Caremark's home infusion business to Coram in April 1995 and involved claims of misrepresentation by each company.
Upon completion of the acquisition, Integrated Health Services will operate more than 700 home health branch locations in 44 states and more than $1.2 billion in home health revenue.
Integrated Health Services offers post-acute medical and rehabilitative services.
